## What it is

A full-size late-1990s/early-2000s corded two-button wheel mouse for the talk's
home-office foreground, proportioned beside a CRT and keyboard. It is a render
asset in millimetres, never a printable part.

## Design notes

The 130 × 69 × 43 mm body uses a smooth ergonomic pebble silhouette with a
rear-biased palm hump, a subtly right-shifted crown, and a shallow left thumb
scallop. The complete asset reaches 185.68 mm because the front strain relief
continues into a short cable lead that drops onto the desk.

Upper and lower mouldings are physically separated by a continuous perimeter
parting gap and joined only by a hidden internal bridge. The centre split reaches
the nose, while a transverse break makes the left and right button caps distinct
from the palm shell. A treaded 17.5 mm dark rubber wheel sits in a rounded well
on an embedded axle.

Four broad glide pads establish the desk plane beneath the raised lower shell.
The underside carries only a restrained optical-sensor pocket; the cable and
ribbed tapered strain relief replace the old wireless battery/receiver logic.

The shell is sampled densely enough to carry a smooth projected silhouette —
eight subdivisions per station pair and 40 profile samples, which is what the
scene's raking key light needs to shade the palm as one continuous moulding —
while keeping the final GLB at 10,012 triangles. Small cable and strain-relief
sections use controlled polygon counts because their analytic CAD equivalents
spent more triangles than the complete finished asset.

```toml
[part]
min_wall = 0.5

[accepted]
# Render-only grooves, wheel tread, cable joins, and sampled end caps earn
# these; the 2026-08-28 densified shell raised the count with the sampling.
sliver = 521
```

## Don't

- Don't restore the wireless hatch, receiver, or cable-free silhouette.
- Don't turn the nose into a pointed gaming wedge or add sci-fi surface panels.
- Don't remove the upper/lower parting gap, full button split, transverse button
  break, wheel well, strain relief, cable, thumb scallop, or glide-pad contact.
- Don't centre and symmetrise the palm crown; the slight rightward mass and left
  thumb relief are intentional ergonomic construction.
- Don't replace the controlled sampled shell with an analytic smooth loft. That
  experiment exported at more than 160k triangles and broke the 10k asset cap.
- Don't act on FDM floating/overhang findings; this is a connected render asset,
  not a printable part. A `solids` finding still indicates a failed union.

## Changelog

- 2026-08-28: doubled the loft sampling (8 subdivisions per station pair, 40
  profile samples) after the 3.5mm ring spacing shaded as contour terraces —
  the "quilted" mouse — under the scene key light. 10,012 triangles, at the
  10k asset cap.
- 2026-08-26: fully replaced the faceted wireless gaming-mouse wedge with a
  period-correct 130 mm corded ergonomic mouse: rear palm hump, asymmetric mass,
  distinct mouldings and button caps, rubber wheel and well, thumb scallop,
  strain relief, short desk-settled cable, sensor pocket, and four glide pads.
